result.summary:
Independently read test/specs/REQ-207.md and test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs (936 lines) in full, and grepped docs/requirements.yaml for REQ-207's actual entry (6 acceptance_criteria) rather than trusting the spec's restatement.

Per-AC coverage check (sub-check a: runnable test present, no unmitigated skip):
AC1 (production-order, 4 expected outcomes) -> describe 'vortex-production-order-above-threshold' (lines 510-568), all 4 outcome_results asserted individually including the load-bearing eo1.observed.assignee_ref=='role-controller' routing check. Runnable, not skipped.
AC2 (supplier-quality-deviation-critical, EO-001 ordering + sub-process) -> describe at lines 573-711. eo_ordering re-derives DateTime.compare(first_ts, second_ts)==:lt from real destructured timestamps (lines 639-642), not just Runner's own verdict; child spawn verified via a real Repo-queried InstanceProjection row, cascaded to completion and re-verified. Runnable, not skipped.
AC3 (false-positive, reaches end-false-positive specifically) -> describe at lines 716-850. See mutation re-run below.
AC4 (entity-list disposition) -> describe at lines 855-935, 3 live signals (File.read!/Regex.match?/File.exists? against real files at test-run time, not hardcoded booleans). Runnable, not skipped.
AC5 (report states closed disposition for all 4 scenarios) -> read test/reports/req207-vortex-scenario-findings.yaml directly: all 4 scenario ids present (vortex-production-order-above-threshold, vortex-supplier-quality-deviation-critical, vortex-supplier-quality-deviation-false-positive, vortex-entity-list-filter-and-page), each carries a disposition field, no gaps -- consistent with test/specs/REQ-205.md's established precedent of not writing a separate ExUnit test against a static report artifact.
AC6 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors) -> re-ran both myself this session (output below), not inherited from either prior agent's claim.
No @tag :skip anywhere in the file (grepped). No 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the spec (grepped).

Sub-check (c) fixture uniqueness: setup block (not setup_all) calls Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug('req207') at line 248, runs per-test -- confirmed by ExUnit setup semantics, no shared hardcoded tenant/slug/id across the 4 describe blocks.

Sub-check (d) self-sufficiency: grepped for setup_all, Process.put, Agent.start, :persistent_term -- none found beyond the per-test setup/on_exit pair. Each test provisions its own tenant schema (Seed.seed_company/1) and tears it down independently in on_exit (teardown/1, lines 419-434) via DROP SCHEMA CASCADE + row deletes scoped to that tenant's own id. async: false is required only because Sandbox.mode(:auto) targets real Postgres, not because tests depend on each other's state. No test reads state left behind by another.

Sub-check (e) no hardcoded secrets: grepped case-insensitively for password/secret/api_key/connection string/postgres:// -- zero matches. Tokens are generated per-test via Identity.create_token/3 against per-test users.

AC3 mutation re-verification (the specific, mandatory independent check) -- reproduced myself, not read from TEST-DESIGNER's report:
1. Baseline: ran `mix test test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs` on the unmodified file. Result: 4 passed, 'Finished in 7.2 seconds (0.00s async, 7.2s sync)'.
2. Applied one of the two mutations TEST-DESIGNER reported (the assertion-isolation one, not the graph-edit one, since the graph-edit mutation's failure mode -- an isolated_node graph-validation error at test setup -- proves the graph shape is load-bearing but does not by itself prove the NEW assertion is what's checking anything): edited line 840 from `assert false_positive_edge["target"] == "end-false-positive"` to `assert false_positive_edge["target"] == "end-closed"`.
3. Re-ran the suite. Result: 3/4 passed, 1 failed, with the AC3 test failing on exactly this assertion: 'Expected the false_positive == true edge to target end-false-positive specifically, not end-closed ...; observed target: "end-false-positive"' at test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs:840. This is a genuine, real assertion mismatch driven by the actual seeded graph data (not a crash, not an unrelated error) -- confirms the assertion is load-bearing and does discriminate a correct routing (end-false-positive) from an incorrect one (end-closed), i.e. it is non-vacuous. It also confirms this assertion checks a DIFFERENT signal than activated_nodes==[] (which is identical for both terminal nodes, per the code read at lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:373-379, dispatch_end/3, confirmed by grepping every event_type append site under lib/letflow/ for a target-node field: none exists) -- the new assertion reads the seeded @simple_supplier_deviation_graph's own edge/condition/target data directly, which is a structurally distinct source of evidence from the runtime activated_nodes signal both the old and new assertions sit alongside.
4. Reverted the edit (git diff on the line, restored 'end-false-positive'). Confirmed clean: `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` returned empty. Confirmed the revert is correct, not just clean: re-ran `mix test test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs` -- 'Finished in 7.2 seconds (0.00s async, 7.2s sync)', 'Result: 4 passed'.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors: re-ran, clean, no output, exit 0.

All 6 acceptance criteria have adequate, independently-verified coverage. No skip-without-counterpart, no TODO, fixtures unique per test, tests self-sufficient, no hardcoded secrets. AC3's non-vacuousness is independently reproduced (not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's claim) with real observed output quoted above, and the mutant probe was reverted and the revert itself verified via git status and a green re-run, per this role's mandatory mutant-hygiene requirement.
